framework: Japan - AI Promotion Act (Act No. 53 of 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: Sets basic principles for AI policy, including that AI R&D and use should be pursued with transparency and appropriate conduct so that misuse (crime, privacy leaks, copyright infringement) is guarded against.
what_is_tested: No testing or evaluation; principle-level only

framework: Japan - AI Promotion Act (Act No. 53 of 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: Government is to collect information on AI trends, analyse cases where AI misuse infringed rights, and give guidance, advice and information to businesses and others based on findings.
what_is_tested: Post-incident analysis of rights infringement cases (not pre-deployment testing)

framework: Japan - AI Promotion Act (Act No. 53 of 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: Government must adopt an AI Basic Plan prepared by the AI Strategic Headquarters and approved by Cabinet.

framework: Japan - AI Basic Plan (Second plan, as of 14 Jul 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Plan calls for proactive evaluation of highly capable frontier AI to deter events threatening national security and for sharing international vulnerability and incident information.
what_is_tested: Frontier AI capability / national security risk evaluation

framework: Japan - AI Basic Plan (Second plan, as of 14 Jul 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Government to build AISI capacity to evaluate AI models, traceability and technical controls such as guardrails, and to link evaluation results to ministry systems and operations.

framework: Japan - AI Basic Plan (Second plan, as of 14 Jul 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: AI Strategic Headquarters to aggregate trends, incidents and evaluation knowledge and build a mechanism for ministries to voluntarily inspect and review AI-related systems.
what_is_tested: Ministry-level voluntary review of AI systems

framework: Japan - Guideline for Ensuring Appropriateness of AI R&D and Utilization (decided 19 Dec 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: Guideline sets a risk-based approach (identify, evaluate, respond according to impact); footnote states it is desirable to combine internal testing with independent external testing such as red teaming.
what_is_tested: Internal and external testing including red teaming
who_tests: Business operators / AI R&D institutions (internal and independent external testers)

framework: Japan - Guideline for Ensuring Appropriateness of AI R&D and Utilization (decided 19 Dec 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: Business operators and R&D institutions are to establish AI governance covering risk identification, assessment and response across design, development, provision and implementation, with monitoring and evaluation involving management.

framework: Japan - Guideline for Ensuring Appropriateness of AI R&D and Utilization (decided 19 Dec 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: National government should address risks when using AI in administration, and each ministry appoints an AI governance officer.
what_is_tested: Not specified; no pre-deployment testing steps stated for government use

framework: Japan - AI Guidelines for Business Ver. 1.1 (MIC/METI)
requirement_paraphrase: AI developers are to consider requirements for performance achievable in unexpected environments.

framework: Japan - AI Guidelines for Business Ver. 1.1 (MIC/METI)
requirement_paraphrase: AI business users are to understand the precision and risks of AI output and confirm risk factors before use.
what_is_tested: User-side confirmation of output precision and risk

framework: Japan AISI - Guide to Evaluation Perspectives on AI Safety v1.10 (28 Mar 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: Evaluation should be repeated rather than one-off, with timing and scope set by phase; methods may be technical (tools, red teaming) or managerial (document and policy review).

framework: Japan AISI - AI Safety Evaluation Environment Task Force Study Report (FY2025, 15 Apr 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Report states evaluation environment (open-source software on GitHub since Sep 2025) operationalises the Evaluation Perspectives Guide and Red Teaming Guide; calls for risk-based minimum and recommended standards by scenario.
who_tests: AISI and Task Force; companies (users of tools)

framework: South Korea - AI Framework Act (AI Basic Act)
requirement_paraphrase: Minister may require data and order investigations, with entry to premises, when violations of Arts. 31(2)-(3), 32(1)-(2) or 34(1) are suspected, and may order stop or correction.

framework: South Korea - AI Framework Act (AI Basic Act)
requirement_paraphrase: Act No. 20676 takes effect one year after promulgation of 21 Jan 2025; amending Act No. 21311 (20 Jan 2026) generally effective 22 Jan 2026, with some provisions six months after promulgation.

framework: South Korea - Enforcement Decree (Presidential Decree No. 36053)
requirement_paraphrase: Large-scale AI safety duty applies at cumulative training compute of 10^26 FLOPs or more, and requires cutting-edge technology with likely widespread impact on fundamental rights; results submitted to Minister.

framework: South Korea - Enforcement Decree (Presidential Decree No. 36053)
requirement_paraphrase: High-impact AI operators must prepare risk management plan, explanation plan and user protection measures, ensure human supervision, retain safety/reliability documentation for 5 years, and publish key elements.

framework: South Korea - Enforcement Decree (Presidential Decree No. 36053)
requirement_paraphrase: Domestic representative required for foreign providers with prior-year revenue of KRW 1 trillion or more, AI-segment revenue of KRW 10 billion or more, or over 1 million average daily Korean users.

framework: South Korea - MSIT enforcement approach
requirement_paraphrase: MSIT announced a grace period of at least one year, during which guidance applies and investigations and fines occur only in exceptional cases such as loss of life or human rights violations.

framework: South Korea AISI (AI Safety Institute)
requirement_paraphrase: Institute works on classifying AI risks (e.g., CBRN assistance, evading human oversight), developing evaluation frameworks, evaluation datasets and tools.
what_is_tested: Frontier risk evaluation frameworks and datasets

framework: China - Interim Measures for the Management of Generative AI Services (Order No. 15, in force 15 Aug 2023)
requirement_paraphrase: Applies to services using generative AI to provide text, images, audio or video to the public in mainland China; R&D not offered to the domestic public is outside scope.

framework: China - Interim Measures for the Management of Generative AI Services (Order No. 15, in force 15 Aug 2023)
requirement_paraphrase: On finding illegal content, providers must stop generation/transmission, remove content, retrain or optimise the model, and report to authorities.

framework: China - Provisions on Algorithmic Recommendation Management (in force 1 Mar 2022)
requirement_paraphrase: Providers must implement entity responsibility for algorithm security, including algorithm mechanism review and technology ethics review.

framework: China - Provisions on Algorithmic Recommendation Management (in force 1 Mar 2022)
requirement_paraphrase: Providers with public opinion or social mobilisation capacity must carry out security assessments under state rules.

framework: China - Measures for Labeling AI-Generated Synthetic Content (Doc. No. Guoxinban Tongzi [2025] No. 2; in force 1 Sep 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: Providers may supply unlabeled content on user request if the user agreement assigns labelling duty, and must keep related logs for at least six months.

framework: China - Measures for Labeling AI-Generated Synthetic Content (Doc. No. Guoxinban Tongzi [2025] No. 2; in force 1 Sep 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: When completing algorithm filing or security assessment, providers must submit labelling-related materials.

framework: China - Interim Measures for Anthropomorphic AI Interactive Services (Order No. 21; promulgated 10 Apr 2026; in force 15 Jul 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Providers must run a security assessment and report to provincial cyberspace authority on launch, major technical change, reaching 1 million registered users or 100,000 monthly active users, or other triggers; assessment focuses on safeguards, training data, extreme-situation response, minors and older adults.

framework: China - Interim Measures for Anthropomorphic AI Interactive Services (Order No. 21; promulgated 10 Apr 2026; in force 15 Jul 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Providers must complete algorithm filing under algorithm rules; national authority promotes an AI sandbox security service platform that providers are encouraged to join for security testing.

framework: China - TC260 AI Safety Governance Framework 2.0 (15 Sep 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: Framework classifies AI safety risks and maps technical and governance measures; reported as precursor to national standards.

framework: China - GB 45438-2025 Labelling Method for AI-Generated Synthetic Content (mandatory national standard)
requirement_paraphrase: CAC commentary describes a mandatory national standard specifying explicit and implicit (metadata) labelling methods, released alongside the labelling measures.
